jobs.title: Executive Director - myPlace Health PACE
jobs.description:
myPlace Health is built around a simple but powerful belief: older adults deserve the support they need to live safely, independently, and with dignity in their own communities. As a PACE (Program of All Inclusive Care for the Elderly) organization backed by SCAN Group, myPlace Health brings together customized medical care, social activities, and daily support for participants and their families – all under one roof.

Our centers are more than healthcare facilities. They are vibrant community hubs where participants are known by name, valued, and supported as whole people. Behind that experience is a dedicated, interdisciplinary team working together to coordinate care, remove barriers, and improve quality of life for some of the most medically and socially complex populations.

For employees, myPlace Health offers the opportunity to do deeply meaningful work in a highly collaborative setting. Team members are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas, and grow alongside a mission that prioritizes compassion, respect, and impact. The result is a culture where people feel connected—to their colleagues, their participants, and the communities they serve.

At myPlace Health, work is more than a job. It’s a shared commitment to honoring what matters most.

Behind that experience is a dedicated, interdisciplinary team working together to coordinate care, remove barriers, and improve quality of life for some of the most medically and socially complex populations.

For employees, myPlace Health offers the opportunity to do deeply meaningful work in a highly collaborative setting. Team members are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas, and grow alongside a mission that prioritizes compassion, respect, and impact. The result is a culture where people feel connected—to their colleagues, their participants, and the communities they serve.

At myPlace Health, work is more than a job. It’s a shared commitment to honoring what matters most.

About SCAN

SCAN Group is a not-for-profit organization dedicated to tackling the most pressing issues facing older adults in the United States. SCAN Group is the sole corporate member of SCAN Health Plan, one of the nation’s leading not-for-profit Medicare Advantage plans, serving more than 300,000 members in California, Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Washington and Texas. SCAN has been a mission-driven organization dedicated to keeping seniors healthy and independent for more than 40 years and is known throughout the healthcare industry and nationally as a leading expert in senior healthcare. SCAN employees are a group of talented, passionate professionals who are committed to supporting older adults on their aging journey, while also innovating healthcare for seniors everywhere. Employees are provided in-depth training and access to state-of-the-art tools necessary to do their jobs, as well as development and growth opportunities. SCAN takes great pride in recognizing our team members as experts in their fields and rewarding them for their efforts. If you are interested in becoming part of an organization that is innovating senior healthcare visit www.thescangroup.org, www.scanhealthplan.com, or follow us on LinkedIn; Facebook; and Twitter.

About MyPlace Health

myPlace Health was founded in 2021 by mission-driven healthcare leaders and organizations that are committed to drastically improving health outcomes, quality and experience for vulnerable older adults and frail seniors. We are an integrated care delivery organization that specializes in providing personalized care and coverage to older adults who wish to remain safely living in their homes and communities for as long as possible, rather than living in a nursing facility.

Our mission is simple: to enable seniors to live the independent lives they deserve. The primary ways in which we pursue our mission are through capitated arrangements with government payers, such as Medicare and Medicaid under the PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) model, and as a value-based provider working in partnership with local health plans.

We are building a mission-driven team that shares our passion for redefining the way older adults experience care as they “age in place” in the community. This is a unique opportunity to take on one of our country’s most challenging healthcare problems and it is a unique moment in time to join us as we scale up to spread our mission across markets.

The Job

The Executive Director is responsible for serving as the senior operating leader for an assigned market, with full accountability for strategy, operations, culture, growth, participant experience, regulatory compliance, and financial performance. In close partnership with the Executive Medical Director, local leaders, and national leadership teams, this role drives the successful execution of the care model to achieve key clinical, quality, member experience, and business outcomes. The Executive Director leads and develops a high-performing market team, builds strong relationships with community and regulatory partners, and ensures the market operates in alignment with organizational goals and PACE requirements. This role is designed for a mission-driven, seasoned operating leader who brings experience leading integrated care operations, ideally in PACE or similar value-based care environments, and who is passionate about improving how care is delivered to vulnerable older adults while helping build capabilities that can scale across markets.

You Will

Serve as the executive operating leader for the market with full accountability for strategy, planning, operations, participant experience, compliance, and overall performance outcomes.

Partner with local and national clinical and operational leadership to drive high-quality care, strong clinical outcomes, participant satisfaction, operational excellence, and regulatory compliance.

Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing, diverse market team, including clinical and operational leaders, to support excellent care delivery and sustainable market success.

Establish, communicate, and model a clear operating strategy and culture vision that promotes accountability, engagement, service excellence, and alignment with organizational goals.

Collaborate with national leadership to implement, optimize, and sustain the infrastructure, systems, and operational processes needed to support all aspects of market performance.

Serve as the local expert in the care model and PACE regulatory requirements, ensuring the market maintains compliance and implements effective operational solutions to meet regulatory and organizational standards.

Oversee market financial performance, including budget development, resource planning, and ongoing monitoring of financial and operational results.

Represent the organization externally by building and maintaining effective relationships with providers, strategic partners, community-based organizations, and regulatory stakeholders.

Identify and advance opportunities to strengthen and adapt the care model to meet local community needs, improve participant outcomes, and leverage strategic partnerships.

Foster a culture of continuous learning, improvement, and operational ownership by leading with flexibility, sound judgment, and a service-oriented approach that supports participants, caregivers, and staff.

We seek Rebels who are curious about AI and its power to transform how we operate and serve our members.

Actively support the achievement of SCAN’s Vision and Goals.

Other duties as assigned.

Your Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Public Health, Gerontology, or a related field required

Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, care delivery, or related business leadership roles

Minimum of 7 years of supervisory, managerial or executive leadership experience

Passion for serving high-risk, vulnerable, and frail older adults

Leadership experience building, scaling, growing, improving, and/or turning around care delivery businesses or clinical business units

Demonstrated understanding of or experience leading care management functions within PACE, Medicaid managed care, Medicare Advantage, or other government-sponsored health plan models

Proven ability to inspire, lead, coach, and mentor high-performing teams in a way that reinforces organizational culture and values

Strong ability to communicate confidently and persuasively with internal audiences

What's in it for you?

Base Pay Range: $150,000-$200,000, Salary + Bonus Opportunity
Work Mode: Onsite
An annual employee bonus program
Medical, Dental, Vision Coverage
Generous paid-time-off (PTO)
11 paid holidays per year, plus 1 additional floating holiday
Excellent 401(k) Retirement Saving Plan with employer match
Robust employee recognition program
Robust Wellness Program
Tuition reimbursement
An opportunity to become part of a team that makes a difference to our members and our community every day!

We're always looking for talented people to join our team! Qualified applicants are encouraged to apply now!

Transform your career with a job that makes a difference in people’s lives!

myPlace Health is building a mission-driven team that shares our passion for redefining the way older adults experience care as they “age in place” in the community. This is a unique opportunity to take on one of our country’s most challenging healthcare problems and join a fast-growing, dynamic team as we prepare to scale our mission to serve more markets.

Learn more about open career opportunities at myPlace Health and to find out how you can join an industry-leading team of clinicians, operators, technologists, and healthcare industry subject matter experts.

If you want to be part of a team committed to drastically improving health outcomes and quality of life for older adults and frail seniors, we want to hear from you!

The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign leads the Sierra Club’s work to achieve an equitable transformation of the power sector away from coal and gas to 100 percent clean energy. This is a senior leadership position within the Sierra Club. The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign serves as the campaign’s lead fundraiser and the primary relationship manager for the foundations and major donors who invest in this work, and is accountable for translating that investment into clear strategy, measurable results, and meaningful outcomes for both communities and donors.

The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign sets high-level power sector strategy, approves local campaign plans, and raises and deploys resources to achieve the organization’s top goals The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign will foster collaboration with Beyond Coal staff as well as teams across other Sierra Club Energy Campaigns and will be capable of managing internal and external opportunities and challenges. The Campaign Director will do all of the above in a way that ensures strategies and tactics leverage opportunities to advance justice (centered on racial justice), equity, and inclusion while building long-term power.

Job activities include but are not limited to:

Lead fundraising for the Beyond Coal Campaign. Serve as the campaign’s principal fundraiser, responsible for securing the revenue that powers the campaign’s annual budget. Build and manage a pipeline of institutional and individual funding prospects; cultivate, solicit, and close six- and seven-figure grants and gifts from foundations and high-net-worth individuals; and partner closely with the Office of Advancement on prospect strategy, proposal development, presentations, and reporting. Set annual revenue goals, own performance against them, and adjust campaign expenses based on quarterly revenue projections and strategic opportunity
Steward the campaign’s donor relationships. Serve as the primary programmatic contact for the campaign’s foundation and major-donor partners. Maintain a proactive cadence of updates, briefings, and meetings; lead the drafting of grant deliverables and reports, and ensure they are completed on time and at high quality; communicate campaign impact and return on investment in terms that matter to each funder; and manage funder expectations through moments of change. Ensure knowledge of each relationship is documented so that it belongs to the institution, not only to individuals
Manage a large, complex budget. Ensure we are providing donors a meaningful return on investment, achieving our stated goals, and aligning resources with strategy on an ongoing basis. Owns strategy and budgetary decisions, deploying resources in service of Beyond Coal Campaign and power sector goals through a consultative and collaborative approach
Lead campaign strategy, planning, design, and evaluation for the Beyond Coal Campaign, centered in equity, justice, and inclusion, that meets the challenge of the current climate crisis. Develop an actionable theory of change, core strategies, and campaign goals and outcomes. Continue to build and elevate the campaign and organization’s work to accelerate the buildout of clean energy, retire existing coal plants, and block new gas plants. Engage across the organization and the movement to ensure the campaign is rooted in equitable outcomes and contributes to building long-term power. Oversee strategic campaign planning at the national level, and support local planning. Approves local plans in partnership with relevant stakeholders
Provide strategic leadership to the Sierra Club and those implementing the Beyond Coal Campaign strategy. The Director will need to effectively delegate, follow-up, and project manage in a rapidly changing environment with competing demands. Serve as the strategic lead and provide guidance to all parts of the Sierra Club and with partners and external stakeholders related to the Beyond Coal Campaign. Accountable for building strong relationships across groups of stakeholders to ensure goal alignment, support for staff engaged in the Beyond Coal Campaign work, and compelling narratives to advance outcomes. Lead the Beyond Coal Campaign team’s engagement with the Field Department and Chapters, Environmental Law Program, Communications, and deputize staff and delegates work as appropriate
Supervise and mentor up to 6 direct reports by setting performance objectives, providing regular feedback, and supporting staff to excel. Effectively manage, guide, and coach staff; ensure individual professional development; establish performance objectives and expectations; and evaluate accomplishments and effectiveness. Take appropriate disciplinary action when needed, and make hiring and termination recommendations. Ensure campaign staff advance assigned projects by collaborating with other Sierra Club staff and volunteers as well as external partners. Establish strategic priorities and monitor progress toward annual results
Serve as a member of the Energy Campaigns Team. Help shape and manage the direction of intersectional energy campaigns, and support a holistic vision for significant greenhouse gas reductions across interrelated sectors of the economy. Support an effective and visionary theory of change for the Energy Campaigns that leverages the power of the campaigns as part of the Sierra Club’s foundational approach to greenhouse gas and harmful pollution reductions while also building power
Serve as a spokesperson. Represent the Sierra Club with the media and with partners as a strategic leader and subject-matter expert on issues related to the campaign
Perform miscellaneous duties as directed

Successful track record of fundraising and donor stewardship. Demonstrated success personally raising significant revenue—including six- and seven-figure grants and gifts—from foundations and high-net-worth individuals, spanning cultivation, solicitation, closing, reporting, and renewal. Experience partnering with advancement or development staff on proposals, presentations, and donor communications. Experience writing successful grant proposals and grant reports, and a record of retaining and growing funder relationships over time, including through moments of organizational or leadership change
Track record of successful organizational leadership or campaign leadership. Demonstrated ability to build, implement, and win strategic campaigns or build successful organizations. Includes identifying a theory of change, leveraging resources both internal and external toward strategies designed to win tangible, meaningful outcomes, and building a team culture that supports success

Strong interpersonal skills to navigate disagreement and lead through uncertainty, ambiguity, or conflict.

Understanding of environmental, climate, and social justice issues and how they relate to each other. Lead the Market. Build the Business. Own the Outcome.

At Haga Kommer, we believe the best leaders don’t simply manage an office. They build people, strengthen client relationships, improve the business, and create opportunities for growth.

We’re looking for a Market Leader who can take ownership of the overall health and growth of a local market. Own something. Build your career. Work across something bigger. Have a life. Help shape what’s next.

We're embracing AI and modern technology to reduce repetitive work, improve research and analysis, and create more time for the work that matters most…solving problems, advising clients, and building relationships.

Continuing education and certification reimbursement

Build a meaningful career without missing the life you're building it for.

We recognize that work and life naturally weave together. Professional success shouldn't require sacrificing the relationships, experiences, and quality of life that matter most.

HK employees are supported by a culture focused on sustainable performance rather than constant burnout.

Hybrid flexibility

COMMUNICATIONS DIRECTOR, REGULATED BOTANICALS AND FUNCTIONAL BEVERAGES– REMOTE

WHO WE ARE

Vivazen launched with a disruptive idea: that a small, plant-powered shot could outperform the synthetic stimulants dominating convenience counters. Over a decade later, we’ve not only proven it; but we’ve also defined the category. As the original brand to bring kratom-based products to market, we’ve since expanded into a powerful portfolio of clean, effective botanical blends with more than 700 million servings sold nationwide.
Retailers rely on Vivazen to drive real revenue in minimal space. Consumers trust us for fast-acting, feel-good energy they can count on. And behind it all is a business built for speed, ownership, and performance.

At Vivazen, you won’t wait for permission or promotion. From day one, you’ll run a real territory with clear goals, visible numbers, and the support to win. As we enter a new phase of rapid growth, we’re building a team that’s as ambitious as the opportunity. If you're motivated by autonomy, accountability, and upward mobility—and you want to help shape the future of natural performance, you’ll go far at Vivazen.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

The Communications Director leads Vivazen’s corporate and brand communications strategy, driving message development, media engagement, communications planning, content development, and integrated campaign execution across earned, paid, owned, social/digital, and stakeholder channels.

This is a hands-on role that blends strategy with day-to-day execution: the Director will bring forward smart ideas, assess how recommendations will land in the broader external environment, and quarterback programs from plan through delivery. Public affairs experience is valuable, but the role is anchored in corporate/brand communications and digital expertise within a highly regulated environment.

Reporting directly to the VP of Communications and Government Affairs and sitting on the Legal and Corporate Affairs team, this position works cross-functionally with commercial, legal, public affairs, government affairs, and marketing partners and collaborates closely with the communications agency of record. We’re seeking a strategic, proactive, solutions-oriented communications leader who operates with independence, strong judgment, curiosity, and agility in a fast-moving, regulated environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop and lead 360-degree communications strategies that align with organizational goals, ensuring cohesive messaging across internal and external audiences and integrating earned, paid, owned, social/digital, and stakeholder channels as business priorities evolve.
Oversee execution of proactive and reactive media engagement, partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to identify opportunities, craft compelling narratives, and secure strategic media coverage that enhances brand credibility.
Serve as a primary author and hands-on producer of the full communications content suite, including press releases, statements, employee communications, suggested social content, launch communications, executive talking points, Q&A documents, speeches, op-eds, briefing materials, and other external-facing collateral.
Own the day-to-day strategy and execution of paid communications and digital efforts, including sponsored content, programmatic advertising, paid media, SEO and GEO positioning, and local or national activations.
Develop and manage owned and social content calendars and integrated communications plans for product launches, corporate milestones, and stakeholder announcements, partnering with cross-functional working groups from planning through execution.
Lead reputation management efforts by tracking company visibility, awareness, media sentiment, and narrative shifts, and using earned, paid, owned, SEO, and GEO insights to strengthen Vivazen’s positioning.
Manage crisis communications readiness and response, anticipating risks, monitoring sentiment, and coordinating real-time communications plans during sensitive or urgent situations with disciplined judgment.
Shape and steward the company’s narrative across channels, including owned digital platforms, social media, thought leadership placements, and public-affairs-facing issues and campaigns when needed, ensuring communications strategies account for the broader external and regulatory environment.
Collaborate with the communications agency of record, setting strategic priorities, providing editorial oversight, and ensuring the agency delivers quality, timelines, and ROI.
Balance competing priorities across corporate, commercial, legal, public affairs, and government affairs functions, making informed decisions that uphold organizational integrity while maximizing strategic opportunities.
Act as a trusted advisor to business and functional leaders, elevating communications thinking, coaching spokespeople, and reinforcing best practices for message discipline, audience engagement, and stakeholder influence. Comfortably engage reporters, consultants, and stakeholders directly, including in ambiguous or uncomfortable situations.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

7–10+ years of progressive experience in corporate, brand, or integrated communications, with demonstrated leadership of high-impact, multi-channel campaigns within complex organizations and working knowledge of public affairs.
Experience in CPG, healthcare, pharmaceutical, alcohol/beverage, tobacco, cannabis, or other highly regulated industries, with a clear understanding of compliance considerations, reputational risk, and stakeholder sensitivity.
Communications or public affairs agency/consulting experience is strongly valued, particularly experience moving quickly, managing multiple priorities, and producing high-quality work across clients or issues.
Proven track record of developing and executing integrated 360-degree communications strategies across earned, paid, owned, social, and digital channels that influence public perception, support business objectives, and deliver measurable results.
Demonstrated senior-level ownership of communications initiatives from strategy through hands-on execution, with the ability to operate independently, bring recommendations forward, and see projects through without relying on a large internal team.
Demonstrated expertise in media relations and narrative development, with the ability to craft compelling messaging, engage reporters directly, manage spokesperson preparation, and drive earned media outcomes.
Experience with paid communications and digital efforts, including sponsored content, programmatic advertising, paid media, SEO/GEO, and social/digital channels.
Experience partnering cross-functionally with legal, commercial, marketing, public affairs, and government affairs teams, balancing business priorities with regulatory and reputational considerations.

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a portfolio of high-visibility materials such as press releases, employee communications, executive talking points, op-eds, crisis statements, social content, and strategic communications plans.

Job Description

This position is based in Abilene, TX and will require relocation if not already based in Abilene, TX.

As Director of Operations, Critical Infrastructure
, you will lead the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of mission-critical electrical, mechanical, and building infrastructure systems supporting OCI data center campuses. This role is accountable for day-to-day operational execution, risk management, maintenance performance, and leadership effectiveness across assigned sites or regions, ensuring compute load is protected and high availability is maintained at all times.

This role directly leads site-level operational leadership for critical infrastructure, including the Site Operations Support Manager – Data Center Facilities, Office & Facilities Coordinator – Facilities Operations, Facilities Operations Manager – Mechanical / Plant Manager, and Facilities Operations Manager – Electrical / Plant Manager, along with their supporting technical teams. The Director is responsible for ensuring these teams operate as one coordinated facilities organization with strong execution discipline, clear escalation paths, and consistent standards across maintenance, incident response, operational readiness, and support functions.

This is a hands-on operational leadership role with direct accountability for operational outcomes. You will partner closely with Engineering, Construction, Training, Vendor Management, Reliability, and Chief Engineering functions to operationalize standards, strengthen maintenance and emergency response programs, and ensure operability and maintainability are built into both current operations and future growth.

Responsibilities

Lead and manage site or regional operations teams responsible for critical infrastructure, including electrical distribution, on-site power generation, UPS, switchgear, cooling systems, controls interfaces, and life safety systems.
Provide leadership across the full site facilities operations structure, including plant operations, maintenance execution, administrative site support, and operational coordination functions.
Own operational readiness, maintenance execution, and incident response performance for assigned campuses or regions.
Enforce consistent execution and continuous improvement of MOPs, SOPs, and EOPs governing maintenance, load transfers, switching, ramp events, restoration, and abnormal operating conditions.
Ensure strong coordination between electrical, mechanical, and site-support functions so operational work is executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with uptime expectations.
Serve as the operational escalation point for major incidents, ensuring timely response, clear communication, root cause rigor, and disciplined corrective action follow-through.
Establish and track operational KPIs related to availability, reliability, safety, maintenance effectiveness, backlog health, incident trends, and readiness.
Partner with training and technical leadership teams to implement and sustain repair, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and emergency response capability across site teams.
Lead vendor oversight and support performance management for OEMs, maintenance providers, service contractors, and operating agreements tied to campus infrastructure.
Drive a strong safety and compliance culture aligned with company standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
Support staffing, hiring, retention, and development of high-performing operations leaders and technical staff across the organization.
Ensure site-support and administrative functions enable effective scheduling, documentation, workflow coordination, and audit-ready operations in support of the critical environment.
Partner with Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Reliability teams to ensure operability, maintainability, and operational supportability are built into new capacity, retrofits, and expansions.
Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure maintenance, capital work, remediation, and operational activities are properly sequenced and executed with minimal operational risk.
Drive continuous improvement across maintenance practices, incident response, work control, readiness processes, and team operating rhythms.

Ideal Candidate Profile

10+ years of experience in mission-critical operations, power generation, utilities, industrial operations, or related uptime-critical environments, including leadership responsibility.
Strong understanding of critical MEP systems and data center operations, including the interaction between electrical, mechanical, controls, and support functions in live environments.
Demonstrated experience managing operational risk and executing in MOP-driven environments.
Proven ability to lead managers, technical teams, and vendor-supported operations in 24/7 critical environments.
Strong experience with maintenance governance, incident response, and operational readiness at site or regional scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities, Operations, or related field preferred; equivalent experience also valued.

Skills And Competencies

Strong operational leadership in mission-critical environments.
Ability to lead through managers while reinforcing accountability, consistency, and execution discipline.
Strong judgment during incidents and abnormal operating conditions.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership skills.
Ability to balance safety, speed, reliability, and long-term maintainability in a live operational environment.
Strong planning, escalation, and organizational leadership capability.
Ability to align plant operations, maintenance delivery, and site-support functions into a cohesive operating model.

Preferred Skills / Certifications

PE license or equivalent certification is a plus.
Experience with regulatory compliance frameworks such as OSHA, EPA, and related operational requirements.
Familiarity with CMMS, SCADA, BMS, EPMS, and power monitoring platforms.
Experience in hyperscale data centers, utility-scale power systems, or similarly complex high-availability environments is strongly preferred.
Experience partnering with Engineering, Construction, Reliability, and Training functions in support of large-scale infrastructure operations is preferred.

Physical Demands / Work Environment

This is a mission-critical onsite leadership role supporting 24/7 operations where continuous uptime is essential. Regular attendance, schedule flexibility, and availability during major operational events are required. To perform these duties, you must be able to move through office, campus, and active operational environments; walk sites; climb stairs; and safely engage in field visibility and incident support activities, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Why Oracle Cloud Infrastructure?

Global impact at scale:
Contribute directly to how mission-critical OCI data centers operate across regions and continents, influencing infrastructure reliability, security, sustainability, and long-term capacity growth.

Technically rigorous environment:
Work alongside experienced engineers, automation specialists, and compliance teams in a rapidly scaling hyperscale cloud infrastructure, where disciplined execution and technical depth matter.

Culture built on operational excellence:
Join an organization that values safety, process rigor, clear accountability, and continuous improvement as foundational to protecting uptime and customer trust.

Long-term career development:
Benefit from internal mobility, role-based technical training, and development opportunities designed for professionals building long-term careers in cloud infrastructure and facilities operations.

Context:
At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice - a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.

The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign leads the Sierra Club’s work to achieve an equitable transformation of the power sector away from coal and gas to 100 percent clean energy. This is a senior leadership position within the Sierra Club. The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign serves as the campaign’s lead fundraiser and the primary relationship manager for the foundations and major donors who invest in this work, and is accountable for translating that investment into clear strategy, measurable results, and meaningful outcomes for both communities and donors.

The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign sets high-level power sector strategy, approves local campaign plans, and raises and deploys resources to achieve the organization’s top goals The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign will foster collaboration with Beyond Coal staff as well as teams across other Sierra Club Energy Campaigns and will be capable of managing internal and external opportunities and challenges. The Campaign Director will do all of the above in a way that ensures strategies and tactics leverage opportunities to advance justice (centered on racial justice), equity, and inclusion while building long-term power.

Job activities include but are not limited to:

Lead fundraising for the Beyond Coal Campaign. Serve as the campaign’s principal fundraiser, responsible for securing the revenue that powers the campaign’s annual budget. Set annual revenue goals, own performance against them, and adjust campaign expenses based on quarterly revenue projections and strategic opportunity
Steward the campaign’s donor relationships. Serve as the primary programmatic contact for the campaign’s foundation and major-donor partners. Ensure knowledge of each relationship is documented so that it belongs to the institution, not only to individuals
Manage a large, complex budget. Ensure we are providing donors a meaningful return on investment, achieving our stated goals, and aligning resources with strategy on an ongoing basis. Owns strategy and budgetary decisions, deploying resources in service of Beyond Coal Campaign and power sector goals through a consultative and collaborative approach
Lead campaign strategy, planning, design, and evaluation for the Beyond Coal Campaign, centered in equity, justice, and inclusion, that meets the challenge of the current climate crisis. Develop an actionable theory of change, core strategies, and campaign goals and outcomes. Continue to build and elevate the campaign and organization’s work to accelerate the buildout of clean energy, retire existing coal plants, and block new gas plants. Engage across the organization and the movement to ensure the campaign is rooted in equitable outcomes and contributes to building long-term power. Oversee strategic campaign planning at the national level, and support local planning. Approves local plans in partnership with relevant stakeholders
Provide strategic leadership to the Sierra Club and those implementing the Beyond Coal Campaign strategy. The Director will need to effectively delegate, follow-up, and project manage in a rapidly changing environment with competing demands. Serve as the strategic lead and provide guidance to all parts of the Sierra Club and with partners and external stakeholders related to the Beyond Coal Campaign. Accountable for building strong relationships across groups of stakeholders to ensure goal alignment, support for staff engaged in the Beyond Coal Campaign work, and compelling narratives to advance outcomes. Supervise and mentor up to 6 direct reports by setting performance objectives, providing regular feedback, and supporting staff to excel. Effectively manage, guide, and coach staff; ensure individual professional development; establish performance objectives and expectations; and evaluate accomplishments and effectiveness. Take appropriate disciplinary action when needed, and make hiring and termination recommendations. Ensure campaign staff advance assigned projects by collaborating with other Sierra Club staff and volunteers as well as external partners. Establish strategic priorities and monitor progress toward annual results
Serve as a member of the Energy Campaigns Team. Help shape and manage the direction of intersectional energy campaigns, and support a holistic vision for significant greenhouse gas reductions across interrelated sectors of the economy. Support an effective and visionary theory of change for the Energy Campaigns that leverages the power of the campaigns as part of the Sierra Club’s foundational approach to greenhouse gas and harmful pollution reductions while also building power
Serve as a spokesperson. Represent the Sierra Club with the media and with partners as a strategic leader and subject-matter expert on issues related to the campaign

Successful track record of fundraising and donor stewardship. Experience partnering with advancement or development staff on proposals, presentations, and donor communications. COMMUNICATIONS DIRECTOR, REGULATED BOTANICALS AND FUNCTIONAL BEVERAGES– REMOTE

WHO WE ARE

Vivazen launched with a disruptive idea: that a small, plant-powered shot could outperform the synthetic stimulants dominating convenience counters. Over a decade later, we’ve not only proven it; but we’ve also defined the category. As the original brand to bring kratom-based products to market, we’ve since expanded into a powerful portfolio of clean, effective botanical blends with more than 700 million servings sold nationwide.
Retailers rely on Vivazen to drive real revenue in minimal space. Consumers trust us for fast-acting, feel-good energy they can count on. And behind it all is a business built for speed, ownership, and performance.

At Vivazen, you won’t wait for permission or promotion. From day one, you’ll run a real territory with clear goals, visible numbers, and the support to win. As we enter a new phase of rapid growth, we’re building a team that’s as ambitious as the opportunity. If you're motivated by autonomy, accountability, and upward mobility—and you want to help shape the future of natural performance, you’ll go far at Vivazen.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

The Communications Director leads Vivazen’s corporate and brand communications strategy, driving message development, media engagement, communications planning, content development, and integrated campaign execution across earned, paid, owned, social/digital, and stakeholder channels.

This is a hands-on role that blends strategy with day-to-day execution: the Director will bring forward smart ideas, assess how recommendations will land in the broader external environment, and quarterback programs from plan through delivery. Public affairs experience is valuable, but the role is anchored in corporate/brand communications and digital expertise within a highly regulated environment.

Reporting directly to the VP of Communications and Government Affairs and sitting on the Legal and Corporate Affairs team, this position works cross-functionally with commercial, legal, public affairs, government affairs, and marketing partners and collaborates closely with the communications agency of record. We’re seeking a strategic, proactive, solutions-oriented communications leader who operates with independence, strong judgment, curiosity, and agility in a fast-moving, regulated environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop and lead 360-degree communications strategies that align with organizational goals, ensuring cohesive messaging across internal and external audiences and integrating earned, paid, owned, social/digital, and stakeholder channels as business priorities evolve.
Oversee execution of proactive and reactive media engagement, partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to identify opportunities, craft compelling narratives, and secure strategic media coverage that enhances brand credibility.
Serve as a primary author and hands-on producer of the full communications content suite, including press releases, statements, employee communications, suggested social content, launch communications, executive talking points, Q&A documents, speeches, op-eds, briefing materials, and other external-facing collateral.
Own the day-to-day strategy and execution of paid communications and digital efforts, including sponsored content, programmatic advertising, paid media, SEO and GEO positioning, and local or national activations.
Develop and manage owned and social content calendars and integrated communications plans for product launches, corporate milestones, and stakeholder announcements, partnering with cross-functional working groups from planning through execution.
Lead reputation management efforts by tracking company visibility, awareness, media sentiment, and narrative shifts, and using earned, paid, owned, SEO, and GEO insights to strengthen Vivazen’s positioning.
Manage crisis communications readiness and response, anticipating risks, monitoring sentiment, and coordinating real-time communications plans during sensitive or urgent situations with disciplined judgment.
Shape and steward the company’s narrative across channels, including owned digital platforms, social media, thought leadership placements, and public-affairs-facing issues and campaigns when needed, ensuring communications strategies account for the broader external and regulatory environment.
Collaborate with the communications agency of record, setting strategic priorities, providing editorial oversight, and ensuring the agency delivers quality, timelines, and ROI.
Balance competing priorities across corporate, commercial, legal, public affairs, and government affairs functions, making informed decisions that uphold organizational integrity while maximizing strategic opportunities.
Act as a trusted advisor to business and functional leaders, elevating communications thinking, coaching spokespeople, and reinforcing best practices for message discipline, audience engagement, and stakeholder influence. Comfortably engage reporters, consultants, and stakeholders directly, including in ambiguous or uncomfortable situations.

7–10+ years of progressive experience in corporate, brand, or integrated communications, with demonstrated leadership of high-impact, multi-channel campaigns within complex organizations and working knowledge of public affairs.
Experience in CPG, healthcare, pharmaceutical, alcohol/beverage, tobacco, cannabis, or other highly regulated industries, with a clear understanding of compliance considerations, reputational risk, and stakeholder sensitivity.

Proactive, curious, solutions-oriented, and comfortable operating in ambiguity; a constant learner and collaborative team player who leads by example.

Job Description

This position is based in Abilene, TX and will require relocation if not already based in Abilene, TX.

As Director of Operations, Critical Infrastructure
, you will lead the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of mission-critical electrical, mechanical, and building infrastructure systems supporting OCI data center campuses. This role is accountable for day-to-day operational execution, risk management, maintenance performance, and leadership effectiveness across assigned sites or regions, ensuring compute load is protected and high availability is maintained at all times.

This role directly leads site-level operational leadership for critical infrastructure, including the Site Operations Support Manager – Data Center Facilities, Office & Facilities Coordinator – Facilities Operations, Facilities Operations Manager – Mechanical / Plant Manager, and Facilities Operations Manager – Electrical / Plant Manager, along with their supporting technical teams. The Director is responsible for ensuring these teams operate as one coordinated facilities organization with strong execution discipline, clear escalation paths, and consistent standards across maintenance, incident response, operational readiness, and support functions.

This is a hands-on operational leadership role with direct accountability for operational outcomes. You will partner closely with Engineering, Construction, Training, Vendor Management, Reliability, and Chief Engineering functions to operationalize standards, strengthen maintenance and emergency response programs, and ensure operability and maintainability are built into both current operations and future growth.

Responsibilities

Lead and manage site or regional operations teams responsible for critical infrastructure, including electrical distribution, on-site power generation, UPS, switchgear, cooling systems, controls interfaces, and life safety systems.
Provide leadership across the full site facilities operations structure, including plant operations, maintenance execution, administrative site support, and operational coordination functions.
Own operational readiness, maintenance execution, and incident response performance for assigned campuses or regions.
Enforce consistent execution and continuous improvement of MOPs, SOPs, and EOPs governing maintenance, load transfers, switching, ramp events, restoration, and abnormal operating conditions.
Ensure strong coordination between electrical, mechanical, and site-support functions so operational work is executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with uptime expectations.
Serve as the operational escalation point for major incidents, ensuring timely response, clear communication, root cause rigor, and disciplined corrective action follow-through.
Establish and track operational KPIs related to availability, reliability, safety, maintenance effectiveness, backlog health, incident trends, and readiness.
Partner with training and technical leadership teams to implement and sustain repair, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and emergency response capability across site teams.
Lead vendor oversight and support performance management for OEMs, maintenance providers, service contractors, and operating agreements tied to campus infrastructure.
Drive a strong safety and compliance culture aligned with company standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
Support staffing, hiring, retention, and development of high-performing operations leaders and technical staff across the organization.
Ensure site-support and administrative functions enable effective scheduling, documentation, workflow coordination, and audit-ready operations in support of the critical environment.
Partner with Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Reliability teams to ensure operability, maintainability, and operational supportability are built into new capacity, retrofits, and expansions.
Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure maintenance, capital work, remediation, and operational activities are properly sequenced and executed with minimal operational risk.
Drive continuous improvement across maintenance practices, incident response, work control, readiness processes, and team operating rhythms.

Ideal Candidate Profile

10+ years of experience in mission-critical operations, power generation, utilities, industrial operations, or related uptime-critical environments, including leadership responsibility.
Strong understanding of critical MEP systems and data center operations, including the interaction between electrical, mechanical, controls, and support functions in live environments.
Demonstrated experience managing operational risk and executing in MOP-driven environments.
Proven ability to lead managers, technical teams, and vendor-supported operations in 24/7 critical environments.
Strong experience with maintenance governance, incident response, and operational readiness at site or regional scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities, Operations, or related field preferred; equivalent experience also valued.

Skills And Competencies

Strong operational leadership in mission-critical environments.
Ability to lead through managers while reinforcing accountability, consistency, and execution discipline.
Strong judgment during incidents and abnormal operating conditions.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership skills.
Ability to balance safety, speed, reliability, and long-term maintainability in a live operational environment.
Strong planning, escalation, and organizational leadership capability.
Ability to align plant operations, maintenance delivery, and site-support functions into a cohesive operating model.

Preferred Skills / Certifications

PE license or equivalent certification is a plus.
Experience with regulatory compliance frameworks such as OSHA, EPA, and related operational requirements.
Familiarity with CMMS, SCADA, BMS, EPMS, and power monitoring platforms.
Experience in hyperscale data centers, utility-scale power systems, or similarly complex high-availability environments is strongly preferred.
Experience partnering with Engineering, Construction, Reliability, and Training functions in support of large-scale infrastructure operations is preferred.

Physical Demands / Work Environment

This is a mission-critical onsite leadership role supporting 24/7 operations where continuous uptime is essential. Regular attendance, schedule flexibility, and availability during major operational events are required. To perform these duties, you must be able to move through office, campus, and active operational environments; walk sites; climb stairs; and safely engage in field visibility and incident support activities, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Why Oracle Cloud Infrastructure?

Global impact at scale:
Contribute directly to how mission-critical OCI data centers operate across regions and continents, influencing infrastructure reliability, security, sustainability, and long-term capacity growth.

Technically rigorous environment:
Work alongside experienced engineers, automation specialists, and compliance teams in a rapidly scaling hyperscale cloud infrastructure, where disciplined execution and technical depth matter.

Culture built on operational excellence:
Join an organization that values safety, process rigor, clear accountability, and continuous improvement as foundational to protecting uptime and customer trust.

Long-term career development:
Benefit from internal mobility, role-based technical training, and development opportunities designed for professionals building long-term careers in cloud infrastructure and facilities operations.
